Interactive D3 lollipop chart

pv_lollipop.Rd

A ranking chart — the bar chart's lighter cousin: one hairline stem and dot per category, drawn horizontally so category names stay upright and readable, with the value at each head. Sorted largest-first by default. Capped at 40 categories, beyond which no ranking stays readable.

Usage

pv_lollipop(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  sort = TRUE,
  value_labels = "auto",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  mode = "auto",
  duration = 600,
  source = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  elementId = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with at most 40 rows (one per category). Rows with a missing category or value are dropped with a warning.

x

Name of the category column.

y

Name of the numeric value column.

sort

Sort categories by value, largest first?

value_labels

Print the compact value at each head? TRUE always, FALSE never, and "auto" (the default) shows them only while the plot area stays at least 200px wide — on narrower charts they cannot fit, so they are dropped and the tooltip alone carries the exact figures.

title, subtitle

Optional chart heading text.

mode

"auto" (default: follow the viewer's light/dark setting), "light", or "dark".

duration

Entrance transition length in ms.

source

Optional source/credit line, shown small and grey at the bottom left — e.g. "Source: Bundesamt für Statistik".

width, height, elementId

Standard htmlwidgets sizing arguments.

Value

An htmlwidget.

Examples

f25 <- pv_fiscal[pv_fiscal$year == 2025, ]
top <- head(f25[order(-f25$equalization_chf), ], 15)
pv_lollipop(top, x = "municipality", y = "equalization_chf",
            title = "Largest equalization payments, 2025")
